title: 第13章 极道修士第14章 符章炼气
content_zh:
玉阶楼台，陆家仙府。
是夜。
突听一声痛呼。
陆明轩坐在蒲团上，突然面色青白一片，手中一卷书册掉落于地，其上赫然标注着《赤松子说不死经》七字鸟篆。
“道经果然不是随随便便就能读的。其中记载着诸多古仙神圣的修行教诲，能引动法力气机异动。若不能明悟道经精髓，贸然翻阅，必然导致气机大乱，有走火入魔的风险。”他调息许久，才缓过神来，面色并不好看。
他抖开手里的道经书页，金箔烫印的卷数在日光下晃眼，陡然转念一想，又是冷笑，“道经为修行根本大经，十二万九千六百卷，正合一元之数，我陆家三代人接力批注，才勘透不过三十来本。”
他脑海中闪过易数课堂上在角落里沉浸道经不止的那道消瘦身影，嘴角勾出冷冷的弧度，“某些人连灵根都没有，捧着本道经啃得香，还杂糅诸多，想走极道修士之路。
却不知道极道王修，要以四书五经为纲，一元道经为目，尽数参透，才有望大成，趋之万法皆具，无所不能的境地。
古来极道修士哪个不是出身仙教大派，哪个不是皓首穷经，往往都半道而废？
一个无根底凡俗出身的修士，恐怕连道经目录都收集不全吧！十二万九千六百卷，对应天地周天之数，少一卷都悟不透圆满！
吴燃灯，你以为写几个字画几道符，就能窥得大道？
不过这吴燃灯沉迷其中倒是好事，荒废修仙和仙业，就对我陆家再也够不成威胁了。
只是这吴燃灯落笔成符的手段，实在玄妙，得想办法弄到其符道心得才好！”
陆明轩心思陡转，目光不由掠向手上的道经，晦暗不明。
……
“道经再多，终究是前人脚印。前人能走通，我必然也行！”
小屋香烛，袅袅青烟带着沁人的香烛，提神醒神，吴燃灯指尖划过“以梅观道，以心契卦。不执卦象，唯取真机”的批注，头没抬起片刻，只有一股信念在回荡。
【梅花定运函经：入门（5100）】
学无止境，下了功夫，必有所得。
这就是他最大的底气所在。

至于极道修士，要不是这陆明轩提及，他倒从未想过。
回来回头一看，吴燃灯反倒认为极其适合自身。
只因这极道修士，是以四书五经为纲，一元道经为目，穷尽世之道理，道理越多，道行越深，从而万法归一，同辈称王，故世称：极道王修。
简而言之就是一句话，读道经，极道修，仙称王！
读书并不能直接助于修行，却能列于修仙十次第五位，更在六名七相之上，或许就是极道读经的缘故吧！
之前吴燃灯还心有困惑，现在已全然明了。
一命二运三功业…修仙十次第，每一项都是修行人的极大助力，缺一项，都会有所限制，道途艰难。
现在能有一条光凭读书，就能通行于世的大道，何乐而不为？
而读书，是吴燃灯最擅长的事了。
“道经在心，不在卷数。”吴燃灯指尖点向自己眉心，“此处若明，一卷《子曰》可通天地；此处若昧，百万卷道经也只是废纸。”
话音刚落，他袖中滑落半张纸，上面是昨夜批注的“格物致知”：“如磨镜，尘去则明，何须计较镜是铜铸还是玉琢？”
想当初，那卷《仙举前尘录》封皮都快被虫蛀了，不也是被他将纸页翻烂，硬生生趟出一条通玄路吗？
路就在眼前，一步一个脚印，只要不停，就是大道！
content_en:
The jade staircase is the Lu family's fairy mansion.
It's night.
Suddenly a cry of pain was heard.
Lu Mingxuan was sitting on the futon, and suddenly his face turned pale and pale. A book in his hand fell to the ground. It was clearly marked with the seven-character bird seal script of "The Sutra of the Immortal by Chi Songzi".
"The Taoist Scripture is indeed not something that can be read casually. It contains many sacred cultivation teachings of ancient immortals, which can trigger changes in magic power and energy. If you cannot clearly understand the essence of the Taoist Scripture and read it rashly, it will inevitably lead to chaos in the energy and there is a risk of going crazy." He adjusted his breath for a long time before he regained consciousness, and his face was not good-looking.
He shook open the pages of the Taoist Scripture in his hand, and the gold foil-stamped volumes dazzled in the sun. He suddenly thought about it and sneered again, "The Taoist Scripture is the fundamental scripture of spiritual practice. There are 129,600 volumes, which is exactly the number of one yuan. Three generations of my Lu family have worked on it to annotate it, but I can't get through more than thirty copies."
The emaciated figure in the corner of Yishu Classroom who was immersed in the Tao Sutra flashed through his mind, and the corner of his mouth curved in a cold arc, "Some people don't even have spiritual roots. They hold this Tao Sutra and chew it up, and they mix it up with many things, and they want to follow the path of an extreme monk.
But they don’t know that the Supreme Dao King Cultivator must take the Four Books and Five Classics as the outline, and the One Yuan Dao Sutra as the goal, and understand them all. Only then can he hope to achieve great success and reach a state where all dharma is available and omnipotent.
Which of the ancient Ji Dao monks was not from a major sect of the Immortal Sect, and which one was not from the Haoshou Qiongjing, but they often gave up halfway?
A monk with no earthly background may not even be able to collect a complete catalog of Taoist scriptures! There are one hundred and twenty-nine thousand six hundred volumes, corresponding to the number of heavens, earth, and circumferences. Even if one volume is missing, one cannot fully understand it!
Wu Randeng, do you think you can get a glimpse of the avenue by writing a few words and drawing a few symbols?
But it's a good thing that Wu Randeng is addicted to it. If he wastes his cultivation and immortality, he will no longer be a threat to my Lu family.
It's just that Wu Randeng's method of writing the talisman is really mysterious, so he has to find a way to get his experience in talismans! "
Lu Mingxuan's mind suddenly changed, and his eyes couldn't help but glance at the Taoist Scripture in his hand, which was dim and unclear.
…
"No matter how many Taoist scriptures there are, they are still the footprints of our predecessors. If our predecessors can walk through it, I can do it too!"
There was an incense candle in the cabin, and the green smoke carried the refreshing incense candle, which refreshed the mind. Wu Randeng's fingertips ran across the annotation "Observe the Tao with plum blossoms, and understand the hexagram with the heart. Do not hold on to the hexagram, only take the true meaning." He did not raise his head for a moment, only a wave of faith echoed.
[Plum Blossom Destiny Letter: Getting Started (5100)]
There is no end to learning, if you work hard, you will gain something.
This is his greatest confidence.
As for the Ji Dao monks, if Lu Mingxuan hadn't mentioned it, he would have never thought about it.
When he came back and looked back, Wu Randeng felt that it was extremely suitable for him.
Just because this Ji Dao monk takes the Four Books and Five Classics as the outline and the One Yuan Dao Sutra as the goal, exhausts the principles of the world. The more principles, the deeper the Tao practice, so that all laws are unified, and his peers are called kings. Therefore, in the world, they are called: Ji Dao King Cultivator.
In short, it is a sentence, read the Taoist scriptures, practice the ultimate Taoism, and become the king of immortals!
Reading does not directly contribute to spiritual practice, but it ranks fifth among the ten times of cultivating immortality, and is even higher than the Six Names and Seven Phases. Perhaps it is because of the extreme reading of scriptures!
Wu Randeng was still confused before, but now he is completely clear.
One fate, two fortunes, and three merits...the ten stages of cultivating immortality. Each of them is a great help to the practitioner. If one is missing, there will be limitations and the road will be difficult.
Now that there is a way to travel around the world just by reading, why not?
Reading is what Wu Randeng is best at.
"The Taoist scriptures are in the heart, not the number of volumes." Wu Randeng pointed his fingertips to the center of his eyebrows, "If it is clear here, one volume of "Confucius" can connect the world; if it is unclear here, millions of Taoist scriptures are just waste paper."
As soon as he finished speaking, half a piece of paper fell from his sleeve. On it was the "Studying Things to Learn" annotated last night: "Like grinding a mirror, the dust will be gone and the light will be clear. Why bother whether the mirror is made of copper or carved from jade?"
I think back then, the cover of the volume "Records of the Immortal's Preface" was almost eaten by insects. Wasn't it because he turned the pages to pieces and forcibly dug out a path to the mysterious world?
The road is right thereIn front of you, step by step, as long as you don't stop, you will be the road!
